verdicts.verdict_reason: Some ML/AI work clearly exists on this exact domain problem: E-nose/PTR-TOF-MS + ML already predicts soy-sauce fermentation stage, NIR+chemometrics monitors moromi in real time, ML estimates maturity-correlated indices, and — notably — the candidate's own cited source already provides an objective moromi-maturity method (SEM+PCAS). Generic multivariate time-series deep-learning forecasting of fermentation from sensor probes (LSTM, etc.) is also established. So the 'no objective method / very-low-AI-penetration' premise is overstated and the broad problem is touched. However, the SPECIFIC technique and framing the candidate proposes — a pretrained multivariate time-series FOUNDATION model (Toto 2.0) doing zero/few-shot, cross-channel forecasting of in-tank fermentation telemetry to project the convergence/ready-window for soy-sauce or miso moromi — returns no prior art: existing soy-sauce ML is stage classification or point quality estimation (not trajectory forecasting), and existing TS-forecasting deep learning is on other fermentation substrates with bespoke (non-foundation) models. The gap is therefore narrowed but not closed: the foundation-model-forecasting-of-moromi-maturity formulation is genuinely new, while the underlying objective-maturity goal is no longer virgin territory.
